title: Week 2 NFL Injury Rundown: Key Hits Impacting the Eagles’ Playoff Push
body:
The Philadelphia Eagles head into their Week 2 matchup with a cascade of injury news that could reshape the team’s short‑term outlook. While the Birds themselves have largely stayed healthy, several of their upcoming opponents have lost key contributors to serious ailments, ranging from torn ligaments to season‑ending fractures. As the Eagles prepare for a critical stretch of games, the absence of these impact players may tilt the balance in Philadelphia’s favor, but the cumulative effect of league‑wide injuries also underscores the volatility that can define a 2026 NFL season.

One of the most significant blows came to the Dallas Cowboys, who will be without tight end Dallas Goedert after he suffered a torn ACL during practice on Tuesday. Goedert, a three‑time Pro Bowler and a primary target for quarterback Dak Prescott, has been a cornerstone of the Cowboys’ passing attack, averaging 6.2 receptions per game and providing a reliable safety‑valve in the red zone. His loss forces Dallas to lean even more heavily on rookie tight end Jalen Cox and the increasingly versatile wideout CeeDee Lamb, potentially limiting the Cowboys’ ability to stretch the field and protect the quarterback against the Eagles’ aggressive pass rush.

The New York Giants also entered Week 2 with a depleted roster after star linebacker Micah Parsons was diagnosed with a season‑ending torn pectoral muscle. Parsons, a defensive leader and the team’s leading tackler, was instrumental in anchoring a Giants front that had been improving under defensive coordinator Wink Martindale. Without his sideline instincts and run‑stopping prowess, New York will likely rely on a younger corps of linebackers, including rookie Darnell Miller, to fill the void. This shift could present an opening for Philadelphia’s defensive line, which has been effective at generating pressure without a dominant pass‑rusher of its own.

In the NFC East, the Washington Commanders lost their top wide receiver, Jalen Williams, to a broken fibula sustained during a special‑teams play. Williams, who posted 78 receptions for 1,025 yards in 2025, was a key component of Washington’s aerial scheme and a frequent target on third down. The Commanders will now have to elevate backup Tyler Hart, whose limited experience could hamper Washington’s ability to keep the ball moving against a disciplined Eagles defense that has already forced three turnovers in the first two weeks.

On the AFC side, the Buffalo Bills saw running back James Miller suffer a severe hamstring strain that sidelines him for at least six weeks. Miller’s 1,200‑yard season last year helped Buffalo maintain a balanced offensive attack, and his absence forces the Bills to lean heavily on rookie running back Zayden Cole and a pass‑first approach. This could benefit the Eagles, who have struggled to contain dynamic rushing attacks and may find Buffalo’s ground game less threatening than anticipated.

Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams lost veteran cornerback Marcus Bennett to a concussion protocol that will keep him out for the remainder of the season. Bennett, a former All‑Pro, was the Rams’ primary defender against deep routes and a key piece in their secondary rotation. His departure opens the door for younger defensive backs, but the loss of veteran leadership could create communication lapses that Philadelphia’s secondary can exploit with its aggressive press coverage.

The Eagles themselves have been relatively fortunate, entering Week 2 with only a minor ankle sprain to safety Jordan Parker and a lingering shoulder issue for quarterback Jalen Hurts that appears manageable. Head coach Nick Sirianni has emphasized depth and adaptability, noting that the team’s “next‑man‑up” mentality will be tested as the schedule intensifies. The convergence of opponent injuries offers a strategic advantage, yet it also serves as a reminder that the NFL’s physical toll spares no franchise.

Looking ahead, Philadelphia’s path to a playoff berth will still depend on its own health and execution. The upcoming weeks feature a mix of favorable matchups against injury‑hit squads and challenging contests where the Eagles must rely on their own talent rather than opponents’ misfortunes. If the team can stay healthy and capitalize on the weakened rosters of its rivals, the Eagles could solidify an early-season lead in the NFC East and set the tone for a competitive 2026 campaign.
